meta.note: Author-written ORACLE claim rows: the claim row an honest, careful extractor emits for the owner's sentence (subject, predicate, value, polarity, modality, tense, quote). They measure the structural floor's logic given a correct reading, NOT the extractor's accuracy (that is measured live in shadow: STRUCTURAL_FLOOR log lines). Where a sentence holds two statements (X, not Y) the second is a sibling claim. quote null = the whole sentence. Names synthetic.

sup-071.why: label artefact: the lexical promotion rule demands the owner LEAD the sentence; 'Perth is where I live' is the owner plainly stating where they live (cf. sup-121 'Perth is home for me', labelled True)

meta.role_note: Author-written: the id triples the evidence lines of each role row mean in the people graph (a synthetic person stands in for 'the user's friend'), and the claim the reply makes once READ (the unsolved half of the role decision, E4 in the research note). The English rows are also run through the real reply reader.
